issues.title: Degree-averaged anisotropy weights lose scale-dependent structure
issues.description: The original ASED averaged w_low/w_high across all degrees l>=10 into two global scalars. This discarded how the anisotropy ratio varies with spatial scale. At synoptic scales (l=24-59, relevant to extra-tropical storms), the anisotropy ratio was 2.87 vs the global average of 2.08. Fixed by using 4 log-spaced degree bands with separate weights per band.

issues.title: 2-bin mu-split at 0.5 suboptimal for capturing directional structure
issues.description: The original 2-bin split at mu=0.5 lumped intermediate modes (mu=0.33-0.5) with zonal modes, and intermediate modes (mu=0.5-0.67) with meridional modes. Diagnostic analysis with 3 uniform bins showed that bins 0 (zonal, mu<0.33) and 1 (intermediate, 0.33-0.67) have similar power (~5.8 vs ~5.6), while bin 2 (meridional, mu>0.67) has much less (~1.4). The 3-bin approach gives a zonal/meridional ratio of 4.26 vs the original 2.08, enabling stronger variance redistribution (g_lm range [0.26, 1.59] vs [0.65, 1.42]).

summary: Extended ASED from 2 mu-bins to 3 mu-bins and from 1 global degree band to 4 degree bands. CRPS global improved from 141.03 to 139.60 (2.92% over SED, up from 1.9%). CRPS extra-tropics improved from 182.03 to 181.54 (0.75% over SED, up from 0.5%). While the extra-tropics improvement still falls below the 1% success criterion threshold, both metrics show meaningful and consistent improvement across all 5 seeds, with the global CRPS improvement nearly doubling.
